chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rib'i ibn Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

a man who has wealth belonging to an orphan, he said: 'If the orphan is in need and has no wealth of his own, then the guardian should not touch (spend) his wealth; and if he trades with it, the profit belongs to the orphan, and he [the guardian] is liable [for any loss].'
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a guardian managing an orphan's money in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiduciary duties of a guardian (wali) regarding an orphan's capital, distinguishing between consumption for necessity and investment for profit. It establishes that while the guardian may use the funds if the orphan is destitute, any commercial venture undertaken with the orphan's wealth places the profit in the orphan's name while the guardian bears the risk of loss (daman), reflecting the Shia juristic principle of balancing protection of assets with prudent management.
